statement: 2020 capture motive service is carried flat through 2050.
rationale: Avoids turning uncertain catch growth into a fishing expansion target; sustainability remains endogenous only through technology choice, not catch volume.
notes: Full-horizon assumption, not a calibration window.

statement: Existing diesel fleet and electric alternative convert final energy to motive service at 0.30 and 0.75 respectively.
rationale: Diesel matches the existing Fiji domestic-navigation service convention; electric value is an engineering prior.

statement: Observed capture service represents 70% utilization of effective base-year capacity.
rationale: Separates stock sizing from technical availability and permits residual stock to idle.

statement: Aquaculture operations use 0.5 kWh/kg harvest before conversion efficiency.
rationale: Fiji reports harvest and electrical upgrades but not facility energy; a deliberately wide engineering prior is required.

statement: Aquaculture service grows 5% per year from the 2020 initial condition.
rationale: A neutral analytical trajectory distinct from the government 2029 production goals.

statement: Diesel and electric aquaculture equipment convert final energy to operations service at 0.30 and 0.75.
rationale: Engineering prior consistent with motive equipment; no fuel share is constrained.

statement: Observed electric aquaculture service represents 60% utilization of effective capacity.
rationale: Allows pumps and hatchery equipment to idle and separates utilization from availability.

statement: Half of reported offshore longline catch enters the modeled processing/cold-chain boundary.
rationale: No complete Fiji throughput split is published; coastal and subsistence catch are excluded from processing demand.

statement: The base stock estimate allocates final energy 80% electricity and 20% diesel, with output/input efficiencies 0.75 and 0.80.
rationale: The FAO process account reports the carrier split; efficiencies translate it to a common useful-service output. The split sizes residual stock only and is not constrained in dispatch.
central_value: electric share=0.80; diesel share=0.20; electric efficiency=0.75; diesel efficiency=0.80

statement: 2020 post-harvest service is carried flat through 2050.
rationale: Keeps the new service sustainability-neutral and avoids an unsupported processing-growth target.

statement: Observed post-harvest service represents 70% utilization of effective capacity.
rationale: Separates effective stock from availability; both diesel and electric residual stocks may idle.

statement: Each of four reported solar freezers is represented by 0.2 kW electrical input and COP 2.0.
rationale: The official report provides count but not rating; the estimate is small and only sizes an idling residual stock.

statement: Capture, diesel/electric post-harvest, aquaculture, and solar-freezer operating lives are 15, 15, 12, and 10 years.
rationale: Engineering stock-turnover priors; uniform-age retirement avoids assuming every observed asset is new in 2020.

statement: Technical availability is 0.90 for capture/aquaculture and 0.95 for post-harvest equipment.
rationale: Technical availability is distinct from the historical utilization used only to estimate residual stock.

statement: Installed useful-output capex is 1000/3000 capture diesel/electric, 1200/1500 aquaculture diesel/electric, 1200/900 post diesel/electric, and 4000 solar dollars per kW; fixed O&M is 5% diesel, 3% electric, and 2% solar of capex annually.
rationale: Screening economics are disclosed analyst estimates because Fiji-specific technology cost schedules were unavailable.
notes: Fuel and grid costs remain in existing carrier supply chains; variable O&M is zero to avoid duplication.
